title: Second stage of labor: fetal descent and birth of baby
description: Learn second-stage anatomy of maternal pelvis, presenting part, station, head rotation, pelvic floor and baby delivery.

questions.question: When does the second stage of labor start and finish?
questions.answer: It begins at complete cervical dilation and ends when the baby is born. The later delivery of placenta belongs to a distinct third stage.

questions.question: How is fetal station described during labor?
questions.answer: Clinical assessment relates the presenting fetal part to the level of maternal ischial spines. The static pelvis plate cannot measure station or show an actual fetus.

questions.question: Why may the fetal head rotate during vaginal birth?
questions.answer: In a typical vertex mechanism, descent and internal rotation help align the presenting head with maternal pelvic dimensions. Birth mechanism and position vary from person to person.

questions.question: Is every second stage a vaginal birth?
questions.answer: No. Delivery route depends on maternal and fetal circumstances, and cesarean birth may be clinically appropriate. A general pelvis image cannot predict the safest route.

questions.question: What does the labor-stage-two picture actually show?
questions.answer: The new digital cutaway depicts a head-down fetus descending into the vaginal birth canal following complete dilation. The baby has not yet been fully delivered, and it is not a photograph or measurement of an individual delivery. A separate existing pelvis image shows nonpregnant skeletal context.
